key_insight: The paper introduces a new notion—epiplexity—that measures the information in data relative to computationally bounded learners, showing that classic measures (Shannon entropy, Kolmogorov complexity) miss what is actually learnable or constructible by realistic algorithms.
problem_solved: Current information measures assume unbounded observers and therefore fail to capture useful, task-relevant, or learnable information for real-world (compute-limited) AI systems; the paper provides a way to evaluate information content under computational constraints.
method: Define a formal information metric (epiplexity) that conditions information content on computational limits and the class of observers/algorithms.
Provide theoretical analysis contrasting epiplexity with entropy and Kolmogorov complexity, identifying cases where deterministic transformations create additional learnable structure.
Develop practical approximations/experiments that demonstrate how epiplexity better predicts learnability and downstream model performance than traditional measures.
impact: Epiplexity gives practitioners a more realistic yardstick for dataset quality, augmentation usefulness, and representational value under realistic compute limits — helping design better data, benchmarks, and learning systems.
visual_elements: Side-by-side diagram: Shannon/Kolmogorov vs Epiplexity — labels showing 'unbounded observer' vs 'bounded observer' and what each captures.
Pipeline illustration: raw data → deterministic transform → epiplexity score → model learnability (arrow showing increased/decreased learnable signal).
Scatter/bar chart: correlation of entropy vs epiplexity with actual model performance on tasks/datasets.
Icon set: stopwatch/compute chip (bounded compute), magnifying glass (useful/learnable info), gears (deterministic transforms)
paper_title: From Entropy to Epiplexity: Rethinking Information for Computationally Bounded Intelligence
paper_authors: Marc Finzi, Shikai Qiu, Yiding Jiang, Pavel Izmailov, J. Zico Kolter
